A 30-year-old male with a known history of Crohn's disease presents for a routine follow-up. Despite
taking mesalamine for the past year, he continues to experience monthly disease flares requiring oral
glucocorticosteroids. On examination, his temperature is 98.4ºF (36.9ºC), pulse is 64/min, blood
pressure is 133/90 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 15/min. Both general and systemic examinations
reveal no significant abnormalities. The physician prescribes a monoclonal antibody that neutralizes
both soluble and membrane-bound tumor necrosis factor (TNF) but does not induce apoptosis in cells
expressing membrane-bound TNF. Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is most likely
prescribed? Answer Choices: (A) Abatacept (B) Golimumab (C) Tocilizumab (D) Ustekinumab (E)
Adalimumab (F) Certolizumab (G) Natalizumab (H) Infliximab (I) Vedolizumab (J) Etanercept
 A. Infliximab
B. Tocilizumab
C. Vedolizumab
D. Golimumab
E. Abatacept
F. Certolizumab
G. Etanercept
H. Natalizumab
I. Ustekinumab
J. Adalimumab
